svg.aria-label: Diagram: which HA VPN topologies earn which availability SLA in Google Cloud, and what each one requires; connecting an HA VPN gateway to one or two separate peer VPN gateways earns 99.99 percent, as does connecting two VPC networks with an HA VPN gateway in each when both gateways are in the same region, while placing those gateways in different regions drops the figure to 99.9 percent and is explicitly not recommended; connecting to Compute Engine VM instances earns 99.9 percent, and connecting to a single VM inherits whatever SLA that one memory-optimized VM instance carries; the requirement for 99.99 percent is a tunnel from each of the two gateway interfaces to the corresponding peer interfaces, with a full mesh explicitly not required and a single tunnel on a single interface explicitly insufficient because the other interface is left unused; the point that VPC networks are global so same-region gateways still reach resources in other regions; and the difference between active-active routing with identical MED values producing equal-cost multipath and active-passive with different MED values using only the highest-priority tunnel, both keeping each tunnel active, with route withdrawal taking 40 to 60 seconds during which packet loss is expected
svg.title: HA VPN topologies and their SLAs: 99.99 percent is a wiring requirement, not a product tier
svg.text: The SLA is not a property of HA VPN. It is a property of how you wired it.
Same product, four topologies, three different numbers — and one that inherits a VM’s SLA.
What each topology earns
99.99% — HA VPN gateway to ONE or TWO separate peer VPN gateways
99.99% — Two VPC networks, an HA VPN gateway in each, BOTH IN THE SAME REGION
99.9% — The same pair of gateways placed in DIFFERENT regions. Explicitly not recommended.
99.9% — HA VPN gateway to Compute Engine VM instances in multiple zones
INHERITED — to a SINGLE Compute Engine VM, the SLA is whatever that one VM carries: the
SLA for a single VM instance of the memory-optimized machine family.
And from #85: ONE active interface earns no availability SLA at all.
What 99.99% actually requires — and what it does not
REQUIRED: a tunnel from EACH of the two gateway interfaces to the corresponding interfaces
on the peer gateway. At least one tunnel on each HA VPN gateway interface.
NOT REQUIRED: a full mesh. Two tunnels from each interface to each peer interface is more
than the SLA asks for on the Google Cloud side. Your vendor may still recommend it.
NOT ENOUGH: one tunnel from one interface. The second interface is left with no tunnel on
it, and that unused interface is precisely why the configuration fails the SLA.
You never need gateways in different regions — and paying 99.9% for them is a choice
VPC networks are GLOBAL resources, so you can use HA VPN to connect resources in different
regions while the gateways themselves stay in the SAME region.
Reach comes from the network (#84’s dynamic routing mode), not from where you put the
gateway. Spreading gateways across regions buys nothing and costs you a nine.
ACTIVE-ACTIVE
• Peer advertises IDENTICAL MED values
on each tunnel
• Imported as dynamic routes with
IDENTICAL priorities
• Egress uses ECMP across both
• Aggregate throughput is the COMBINED
throughput of both tunnels
• Lose one and you lose that capacity
ACTIVE-PASSIVE
• Peer advertises DIFFERENT MED values
on each tunnel
• Imported with DIFFERENT priorities
• Egress uses the HIGHEST-priority route
while its tunnel is available
• Effective throughput is CUT IN HALF
versus two active tunnels
• One tunnel can absorb all egress
Both modes keep BOTH tunnels active. The difference is MED, not whether a tunnel is up.
That is the naming trap: “passive” does not mean a standby tunnel waiting to be built. It
means an established tunnel that loses the priority comparison.
What the SLA does not promise: a seamless failover
Route withdrawal can take 40–60 SECONDS, and packet loss is EXPECTED during it.
Tunnels restart by themselves, and a failed virtual VPN device is replaced automatically with
the same configuration — but the routing table still has to catch up.
